[EVENT] User had an interview at the US Citizenship and Immigration Services office today.  
[USER] User was nervous but relieved to have the interview over with.  
[USER] User is looking for advice on job searching.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Congratulations on completing the interview at the US Citizenship and Immigration Services office!  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for tailoring a resume to the US job market:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Use a reverse chronological format.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Keep it concise and to the point (1-2 pages).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Use keywords and phrases from the job posting.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Quantify achievements (e.g., "Increased sales by 25% in 6 months").  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Emphasize transferable skills.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Include relevant sections (summary, education, work experience, skills, certifications).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Use action verbs (e.g., "Managed," "Created," "Developed").  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. Proofread and edit multiple times.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 9. Tailor your resume to each job.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 10. Get familiar with US job market norms.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Additional tips: Use a standard font (Arial, Calibri, Helvetica, size 10 or 11), use bullet points, include LinkedIn profile, be prepared to explain gaps in employment.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] By following these tips, you'll be well on your way to creating a US-style resume.  
[USER] User found the resume tips helpful and wants to know more about preparing for a job interview in the US.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Preparing for a job interview in the US is crucial. Tips include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Research the company.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Review the job description.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Prepare your stories using the STAR method (Situation, Task, Action, Result).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Practice your responses.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Dress professionally.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Common interview questions include:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Can you tell me a little about yourself?
